categories.name: Performance
categories.description: Nights on stage and mornings in the field.

posts.title: The ten-minute walk
posts.excerpt: Every rehearsal starts the same way: crossing the studio, heel by heel, in ten minutes.
posts.content:
The studio is twenty-two metres long. Walking it normally takes fifteen seconds. We take ten minutes, and nobody is allowed to stop.

At first the legs shake and the mind runs ahead. Around the fourth minute something gives way, and the floor starts to feel like water.

posts.title: Mixing the white
posts.excerpt: Rice powder, water and a little glue: the paint we wear is made fresh before every show.
posts.content:
Two hours before the doors open, the kitchen smells of wet rice. We stir the white in a wide bowl until it falls from the brush like cream.

Painting takes forty minutes. We help each other with the backs and leave the hands for last, because they crack first.

posts.title: Open studio Thursdays
posts.excerpt: Anyone can come on Thursday evening. Most people arrive curious and leave lying very still.
posts.content:
Last week we had a nurse, two students, a retired carpenter and a boy of eleven. Nobody needed to know what butoh was.

We lie on the floor, lift one arm for five minutes and let it fall. Then tea. That is the whole class, and it is enough.
